Smoke Gets In Federal Eyes

A LOT OF people long have suspected
that federal bureaucracy spells confusion
in a lot of cases.
Exhibit A for today:
Uncle Sam can't seem to make up his
mind whether cigaret smoking is good or
Our government is quietly spending tax-
payer funds to subsidize cigaret commercials
with the aim of selling more American to-
bacco abroad.
This is part of the “product development”
rogram of the Foreign Agricultural Service,
a branch of the U.S. Department of Agri:
culture,

Meanwhile, just 770 paces down the

street, a newly-created Public Health Service
agency, the National Clearinghouse on
‘Smoking and Health, is working hard to
combat cigaret smoking at home,

This effort was authorized by Congress
after an official U.S. commission pronounced
Gigarets to be a “health hazard” in early
1964.
For a time after the official smoking re-
Port, Sec. of Agriculture Orville Freeman
banned new government-sponsored cigaret
promotions abroad. About six months ago,
however, commitments began to be approved
again.
Will the “real” federal authority on cigaret
smoking please stand up? .
